summary: The 13th Dalai Lama worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Agvan Dorjiev, Terton Sogyal, Pa Ri Rabsal, Lobsang Lungtok Tenzin Thinley, Gendun Tendzin Gyatso, Jampa Gyatso, Ngawang Pelden Chokyi Gyeltsen, and Yeshe Chopel.

Working in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology, he studied under Tsenshab Serkong Rinpoche, Trijang Rinpoche, Khunu Rinpoche, Trulshik Rinpoche, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and Ling Rinpoche. In 1989, he founded the International Network of Engaged Buddhists.

Specializing in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies, he studied under Jamphel Yeshe Gyaltsen, Tagdrag Rinpoche, Ling Rinpoche, and Trijang Rinpoche. He founded the Mind and Life Institute in 1990.
The 14th Shamarpa Mipham Chökyi Lodrö was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche, and Kalu Rinpoche (1973).
The 19th Kushok Bakula Rinpoche worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Jamphel Yeshe Gyaltsen (~1930–1941), Ngawang Lobzang Gyatso, and Khangsar Dorje Chang.

id: P:3rd Sras Rinpoche Thubten Kalsang Bstanpai Gyaltsen
summary: A scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he studied under the 96th Ganden Tripa Thubten Kunga, at Drepung Loseling Monastery (1950–1971), and Gyume Tantric College (1971). He held posts at Drepung Loseling, Gyume Tantric College, and Rizong Monastery.

id: P:7th Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche Karma Sungrab Ngedön Tenpe Gyeltshen
summary: Working in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he founded Nitartha International and Nalandabodhi. He also served as director at the Kamalashila Institute.
A Drö Khenpo Yeshe Gyatso studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Thubten Chökyi Dorje.
A Dzom Gyalsé Gyurmé Dorjé was active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, Thubten Chökyi Dorje, and Ayu Khandro.
Krishnaswami Ayyangar studied at Pachaiyappa's College (~1907–1911). He worked at Pachaiyappa's College from 1911 to 1918 and served as a professor at the University of Mysore from 1918 to 1947.
An Indologist, Gajendragadkar served as a Senior Dakshina Fellow at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute and as a Lecturer on Sanskrit at Karnatak Arts College Dharwad.

Muller specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and computational studies. Educated at Stony Brook, Virginia, and Dayton, he taught at Toyo Gakuen University (1994–2008) and the University of Tokyo (2005–2019), and directed Musashino University's Buddhist culture institute.
Working in Indology, Mohan studied under Tirumalai Krishnamacharya from ~1971 to 1989. In 1976, he founded the Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram.

Sabra specialized in philosophy and history/archaeology. He studied at Alexandria University and under Karl Popper at the London School of Economics/University of London (~1950–1955), later holding posts at the Warburg Institute (1962–1972) and Harvard University (1972–1996).

An Indologist and linguist, Ramanujan studied at Mysore and Indiana University Bloomington. He taught at Baroda, Deccan College, and Harvard, and held multiple professorships at the University of Chicago between 1962 and 1993.

Warder worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate at SOAS University of London under John Brough (~1949–1954), later holding posts at the University of Edinburgh (1955–1963) and the University of Toronto (1963–1990).

Narasimhia worked in linguistics and Indology. He earned his PhD at SOAS under Ralph Lilley Turner (~1930–1933) and held posts at the University of Mysore and its Maharaja's College as librarian and part-time professor of philology.
An Indologist, Kathavate succeeded Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar and served as Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 2026).
Barber, a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies, completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison by 1984 and held a post at the University of Calgary (attested 1998).

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology, Proffitt studied at Colorado Boulder, the Inter-University Center, and the University of Michigan under Micah L. Auerback. Around 2015, he became assistant professor of Japanese Studies at University at Albany, SUNY.
